title: Marketing, audit and planning reports: info sheet entries

entries.title: Post the marketing spend of form 17-1 to the books
entries.what_it_does: When ON, approved 17-1 lines paid from bank, mobile or card are written to the journal (Dr marketing expense, Cr bank or mobile), except lines that look like the same spend already in a 11-1 voucher or quick expense, which wait for a person's decision.
entries.why_it_matters: Today marketing spend in 17-1 never reaches the journal profit. Posting it blindly would count the same money twice when it is also typed in 10-2.
entries.default: OFF. Nothing is posted (today).
entries.what_changes_if_switched: Switch it ON only after setting the start date below. Use the 'Post to the books' tab: Dry run first, then Post now. Imprest-paid lines and owner-money lines are never posted by this switch. 'Wind down' moves everything back to zero.
entries.who_can_change: Only the owner (Settings). Posting is run by the accounts manager.

entries.title: Marketing spend is posted from this date
entries.what_it_does: The first date an 17-1 line may be posted.
entries.why_it_matters: Stops old months from being posted into closed books.
entries.default: Blank. The switch above cannot be turned on.
entries.what_changes_if_switched: Lines dated before it are never posted.

entries.title: Repeat purchase window after a promotion (days)
entries.what_it_does: How many days after a promotion ended a later bill counts as a repeat purchase.
entries.why_it_matters: A repeat-purchase figure is meaningless without saying how long we waited.
entries.default: Blank. The report asks the person to type the days; nothing is assumed.
entries.what_changes_if_switched: With a number set, the report uses it when no days are typed.

entries.title: Forecast window (days of history)
entries.what_it_does: How many completed days the sales, item and expiry forecasts look back over.
entries.why_it_matters: More history is steadier, less history reacts faster. The right length is the owner's judgement.
entries.default: Blank. Each forecast page asks for the days; nothing is assumed.
entries.what_changes_if_switched: With a number set, forecasts use it when no days are typed.

entries.title: Day of the month salaries are usually paid
entries.what_it_does: Lets the expected cash calendar put the next salary payment on a date.
entries.why_it_matters: Without a day the salary has no date and is shown as 'date unknown'.
entries.default: Blank. Salary shows as date unknown.
entries.what_changes_if_switched: Unpaid approved payroll is placed on that day; if nothing is owed, the last payroll run is repeated on that day and marked as an assumption.

entries.title: Campaign list
entries.what_it_does: The master list of marketing campaigns with start, end, budget and channel.
entries.why_it_matters: 17-1 lines, bills and online orders point to a campaign here; without it no report can work per campaign.
entries.default: Empty. The owner enters every campaign.
entries.what_changes_if_switched: Nothing is posted or changed by the list itself.
entries.who_can_change: The owner or the people who manage the list.

entries.title: Spend by campaign (#164)
entries.what_it_does: Paid 17-1 amounts by campaign and month, with budget used.
entries.why_it_matters: Shows what each campaign cost. Lines with no campaign stay unassigned; value without payment (samples) is shown apart.
entries.default: Open to the owner, report_marketing and view_reports.
entries.who_can_change: Read only. Export needs export_data and is logged.

entries.title: Spend vs sales (#165)
entries.what_it_does: Marketing spend and bill totals of the same day and place, side by side.
entries.why_it_matters: Shows what happened together. It does not say one caused the other.
entries.default: Open to report readers.

entries.title: Campaign revenue and contribution (#166)
entries.what_it_does: Net sales, discount and contribution of bills tagged with a campaign, next to the campaign spend.
entries.why_it_matters: Untagged sales are never guessed into a campaign, so the share of bills with a tag is always shown. Contribution is on the items whose cost price is known.
entries.default: Open to report readers; cost columns need the cost right.

entries.title: Discount campaign performance (#167)
entries.what_it_does: Bills with a discount grouped by campaign, next to the average bill without a discount.
entries.why_it_matters: Helps see whether discounts go with bigger bills. A comparison is not proof.
entries.default: Open to report readers.

entries.title: Coupon and offer usage (#168)
entries.what_it_does: Uses of coupons from the coupon module (CRM-F) when installed, and codes typed on bills.
entries.why_it_matters: No second coupon system exists here. Typed codes are only labels and are never validated.
entries.default: Open to report readers.

entries.title: Customer acquisition cost (#169)
entries.what_it_does: Marketing spend divided by new customers, by customer source.
entries.why_it_matters: The share of new customers with a source filled is always shown; without a source the spend cannot be split.
entries.default: Open to report readers.

entries.title: Repeat purchase after a promotion (#170)
entries.what_it_does: Of the customers who bought on a promotion bill, how many bought again within the days given.
entries.why_it_matters: A window not yet over shows no percentage, only 'so far'.
entries.default: Open to report readers.

entries.title: Marketing ROI (#171)
entries.what_it_does: Contribution of tagged sales against the spend of the same campaign.
entries.why_it_matters: Only attributable data is used. When an input is missing the figure is blank and the reason is shown.
entries.default: Open to report readers; needs the cost right for ROI.

entries.title: Post 17-1 to the books
entries.what_it_does: Shows each approved 17-1 line and what would happen to it before anything is posted.
entries.why_it_matters: Prevents counting the same spend twice with form 10-2.
entries.default: Preview always available; posting only when the setting is ON.
entries.who_can_change: The accounts manager runs it; the owner winds it down.

entries.title: Audit log (#173)
entries.what_it_does: Everything the system wrote, newest first, with filters, paging and a full CSV.
entries.why_it_matters: The log cannot be edited or deleted.
entries.default: Owner only.
entries.who_can_change: Read only. Each export is itself logged.

entries.title: Voids, reversals and corrections (#182)
entries.what_it_does: Every void, journal reversal and correction of every module in one list.
entries.why_it_matters: Nothing is hard-deleted; modules that never stored the time of a void show a blank time. Salary-related lines are hidden from people without salary view.
entries.default: Open to the owner, report_control and view_reports.

entries.title: Approval delays (#180)
entries.what_it_does: Hours from request to decision by kind and approver, and the oldest requests still waiting.
entries.why_it_matters: Clock hours only; no limit for 'late' is invented.
entries.default: Open to report readers.

entries.title: Stock adjustment approval history (#174)
entries.what_it_does: Wastage, count adjustments and transit losses: who asked, who approved, how long it took.
entries.why_it_matters: Entries made directly have no request and so no approver; this shows which.
entries.default: Open to report readers; values need the cost right.

entries.title: Discount and price-override approvals (#175)
entries.what_it_does: Per bill, who approved a discount and who approved a price change.
entries.why_it_matters: The approver of a price change is stored from this update onward; older bills say 'not captured'. Nobody is guessed.
entries.default: Open to report readers. A new silent capture runs on every bill with a changed price; it never blocks a sale.

entries.title: Voids, refunds and unusual transactions (#176)
entries.what_it_does: Bill voids, voided payments, returns, refunds paid, voided returns and bill exceptions together.
entries.why_it_matters: Events of known kinds; nothing is picked by an amount limit.
entries.default: Open to report readers.

entries.title: User activity (#177)
entries.what_it_does: Per person: bills, voids, returns, forms and (owner only) logins and audit-log actions.
entries.why_it_matters: Counts are not a judgement of the person. Login and audit data come from owner-only tables.
entries.default: Open to report_control readers for business columns; owner for the rest.

entries.title: Missing cost, recipe, batch and expiry data (#183)
entries.what_it_does: Lists items with no cost price, finished goods with no recipe, recipe lines with no waste %, ingredients with no cost and batches with no expiry date.
entries.why_it_matters: A missing cost is never shown as 0; this list shows where that happens.
entries.default: Open to control and stock report readers.

entries.title: Sales forecast (#184)
entries.what_it_does: Coming days estimated from the average of the same weekday in the look-back window, with the lowest and highest as a range.
entries.why_it_matters: The range is not a confidence interval and no probability is claimed. Days with no bill are closed, not zero. A day with no history has no figure. The panel shows the window, trading days, same-weekday days used and data coverage.
entries.default: Needs a window (typed or set); nothing is assumed.

entries.title: Item demand forecast (#185)
entries.what_it_does: Units per item for the coming days from the stock ledger, same method as the sales forecast.
entries.why_it_matters: Days out of stock count as zero, so demand may be understated; items that are not stock-tracked are not covered.
entries.default: Needs a window; nothing is assumed.

entries.title: Production requirement (#186)
entries.what_it_does: For one place: expected demand (and open orders) minus stock on hand = what to make, in units and recipe batches.
entries.why_it_matters: Adding open orders may count some demand twice, so the two columns are separate.
entries.default: Needs a window and a place.

entries.title: Raw material purchase forecast (#187)
entries.what_it_does: The production quantities pushed through the recipes: need, stock on hand and shortfall per ingredient, with cost for people who may see costs.
entries.why_it_matters: A blank waste % is used as zero and flagged; an ingredient with no cost is counted, not priced.
entries.default: Needs a window and a place.

entries.title: Expected cash in and out (#188)
entries.what_it_does: Known future money by day: order balances, customer dues, supplier bills, salary, bank charges.
entries.why_it_matters: An unknown date is shown apart, never placed on the calendar. No opening balance, forecast sales or tax is included.
entries.default: Open to cash report readers; salary lines need salary view.

entries.title: Upcoming supplier payments (#189)
entries.what_it_does: Open supplier bills with due date = bill date + credit days: overdue, coming up, date unknown.
entries.why_it_matters: A supplier with no credit days has no due date; enter it on the supplier.
entries.default: Open to cash and purchase report readers.

entries.title: Expiry and wastage risk (#190)
entries.what_it_does: Batches expiring soon: units expected to sell before expiry (oldest first) and units left over.
entries.why_it_matters: 'At risk' is what is left after expected sales, not a prediction of waste. Batches with no expiry date are not covered.
entries.default: Needs days and a window; the existing setting report_expiry_soon_days can supply the days.

entries.title: What-if scenario (#192)
entries.what_it_does: A past period's real figures with the percent changes you type applied.
entries.why_it_matters: Arithmetic on your numbers, not a forecast; no percent is suggested. 'Result after costs' shows only when every part is captured.
entries.default: All blank = the baseline.

entries.title: Seasonal and festival demand (#193)
entries.what_it_does: For each past festival the owner entered: sales per trading day during it against ordinary days before it, plus sales by month.
entries.why_it_matters: Observed differences are history, not promises; the days behind each figure are shown.
entries.default: Needs the festival calendar.

entries.title: Festival calendar
entries.what_it_does: The owner's list of festivals with dates and an optional uplift %.
entries.why_it_matters: Festival days are left out of ordinary averages; an uplift is shown only when the owner types one.
entries.default: Empty. Nothing is pre-filled.
entries.what_changes_if_switched: Forecasts mark festival days and apply the owner's uplift separately.
entries.who_can_change: Only the owner. Entries are retired, never deleted.
